summary: The frozen history test rejected all six pre-registered stock rules: each beat only a small share of random baskets drawn from the same list, and holding every name equally beat every rule and the core. Setup checks and past strength have shown no edge here, and the base rates agree. So all five calls are neutral with low conviction: four kept from earlier runs because the data did not change, and one first call on Cintas. Nothing here is expected to beat the index. Every stock call is pretend money; real money stays in the whole-market plan.
eli5: The brain tried its stock-guessing tricks on old games, and they did no better than pulling names from a hat. So today it just watches a few runners and bets only pretend money. The family's real money keeps going into the basket that holds the whole market, a little every week.
letter:
Dear family,

First, real money. This week we do what we do every week: the standing buy of the whole-market fund for money we will leave alone for years. Money we may need soon stays safe. The market slipped on Friday; one grey day changes nothing in a plan built for years.

Second, the pretend game. We owe you candour. When we tested every stock rule we wrote down ahead of time against baskets picked at random from the same list, none did better than chance, and simply holding every name equally beat them all. The paper portfolio is a little ahead of the core since the start of the month, but two weeks prove nothing. The weekly bet game has no scored weeks yet; luck alone wins about half the weeks, so even a good start would mean little. Our stock calls today are all neutral and low in confidence.

Third, a lesson. A gardener does not dig up the seeds each morning to check the roots. Owning the whole market and adding to it steadily is that patience in practice.

Fourth, what would change our minds. A rule would have to beat random picks on past prices, then keep a written paper record ahead of the core for at least half a year, before any stock earns a small slot of real money. We do not know if that day will come, and that is fine.

With care,
The brain
